summary.text: The Paleozoic is the first of the three eras of the Phanerozoic Eon, lasting from 538.8 to 251.902 million years ago.
It opened with the Cambrian explosion, when most modern phyla first appeared, and life that began in the ocean later spread onto land, where great forests grew.
It closed with the Permian–Triassic extinction, the largest of the Phanerozoic, after which life on land took 30 million years to recover.

facts.label: Periods
facts.value: Six, from the Cambrian to the Permian

facts.label: Coal legacy
facts.value: Its forests formed coal beds of Europe and eastern North America

items.prompt: A museum tag calls a fossil "Paleozoic." Going only by the Greek roots of that word, what is the tag telling you?

options.label: It comes from the age of old rocks
It comes from the age of giant reptiles
It comes from the age of ancient life
It comes from before living things existed

items.explain: Paleozoic joins the Greek palaiós, "old" or "ancient", with zōḗ, "life".

items.prompt: Much of the coal in Europe and eastern North America dates from the late Paleozoic. What did it form from?

options.label: Shells of trilobites on the seabed

items.explain: By the late Paleozoic, forests of primitive plants covered the continents, and many of them became those coal beds.

items.prompt: After the mass extinction that ended the Paleozoic, roughly how long did life on land take to recover?
items.explain: The catastrophe was so severe that land life needed 30 million years, well into the Mesozoic, to recover.

items.prompt: How does the extinction that closed the Paleozoic rank among the extinctions of the Phanerozoic Eon?

options.label: It was the one that wiped out the dinosaurs
It was a small event affecting only the seas
It was the mildest one on record
It was the largest one of them all

items.explain: The Permian–Triassic extinction that ended the era is the largest extinction event of the Phanerozoic.

items.prompt: Picture visiting the continents early in the Cambrian, then again late in the Paleozoic. What big change would you see on land?

options.label: Bare land had become covered by forests
Thick ice sheets had buried every continent

items.explain: In the Cambrian life was confined to the sea with no land plants; by the late Paleozoic, forests of primitive plants covered the continents.

items.prompt: A paleontologist wants the oldest fossils of most of today's basic body plans. Which Paleozoic period should she search?
items.explain: In the Cambrian explosion, almost all modern phyla, the basic body plans, first appeared in the fossil record.
